facts.value: Restorative justice was developed in the 1970s, though many of its tenets come from Indigenous justice practices.
facts.programme_association: Justice Studies Major – Bachelor of Science

facts.value: Restorative justice focuses on helping victims of crimes, but it also wants to help offenders understand the harm they’ve caused.
facts.programme_association: Justice Studies Major – Bachelor of Science

facts.value: The goal is repair, not punishment.
facts.programme_association: Justice Studies Major – Bachelor of Science

facts.value: Engagement, accountability, cooperation, and community are all essential principles.
facts.programme_association: Justice Studies Major – Bachelor of Science

facts.value: Restorative justice practices have been used in many criminal justice cases, but they’ve also been adopted during conflicts involving families, schools, and workplaces.
facts.programme_association: Justice Studies Major – Bachelor of Science

facts.value: Unlike retributive justice, restorative justice doesn’t focus on what criminals deserve, but rather on what victims need to heal and what communities can do to prevent re-offending.
facts.programme_association: Justice Studies Major – Bachelor of Science
